newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 ends higher as bank stocks surge.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 ends higher as bank stocks surge.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index finished higher for the eighth consecutive session on Thursday boosted by sharp gains in banking stocks and a firm start in New York.
But traders said gains were capped in the run-up to next Thurday's election and volume remained slim at 699 million.
"We are struggling at the 4,400 level," one dealer said. "There was a lack of follow-through buying today and things were dampened by the bond market which was very dull."
The leading index ended just 0.8 points firmer at 4,388.5 after earlier touching 4,400.4.
The broader market remained subdued. Bank stocks featured as investors sought to increase their weighting in the sector which squeezed prices sharply higher.
"The bank sector has kept the market going," another dealer said. "It certainly improved sentiment."
The Mid-250 index finished 11 points lower at 4,517.4.

Gilt futures provided little support, tracking European markets and ending half a percentage point lower as a French opinion poll suggested the centre-right coalition had a wafer-thin lead over the opposition in France's recently-called snap election.
A weaker U.S. bond market further dampened sentiment.
UK shares had opened weaker but strong financials and an expected higher opening in New York had lifted the mood.
The Dow surged at the opening as IBM stock leapt after its earnings outpaced analysts expectations. But by the London close the Dow had lost its 77-point lead and was down two points.
"We anticipated what would happen on Wall Street," said one dealer. "And we didn't react until we knew those gains could be sustained."
Investors preferred to exercise caution so close to the election on May 1 and the possibility of an interest rate rise soon after.
But Chris Chaitow, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities said the FTSE 100 may still reach its all-time closing high of 4,444.3 over the next few days.
"The market is well supported," he said. "The flotation of Alliance & Leicester has been a feature and it's a chance for the institutions to get money into the market."

Among individual share movers Barclays finished 48p higher at 11.06-1/2 stg. NatWest added 19-1/2p to 720-1/2, Lloyds TSB put on 14-1/2p to 551-1/2p, Bank of Scotland gained 18-1/2p to 357p and newly quoted Alliance & Leicester shares were up 7-1/2 to 552-1/2p.
Elsewhere, engineering stocks were depressed after a profits warning from Vickers Plc. The company said the strength of sterling was causing difficulties and export orders were harder to obtain.
Shares in Vickers finished 23-1/2p lower at 202-1/2, TI fell 24 to 523-1/2p and Siebe lost 20-1/2p to 934-1/2p.
